description: Entry schema for a saved reference library. Every category file uses these fields so entries stay human-editable and machine-checkable.

fields.name: id
fields.notes: Stable short id, e.g. src-0001. Never reused after merge.

fields.name: title
fields.notes: Human title exactly as shown by the publisher.

fields.name: url
fields.notes: Exact URL. Canonical form is preferred; tracking parameters are stripped on dedupe.

fields.name: category
fields.notes: Library file slug, e.g. general, technology, legal-policy.

fields.name: tags
fields.notes: Lowercase topical tags used for retrieval.

fields.name: source-type
fields.notes: Shape of the source, not its quality.

fields.name: authority
fields.notes: Trust tier used for ordering and review priority.

fields.name: added-by
fields.notes: Person or agent that added the entry.

fields.name: last-checked
fields.notes: YYYY-MM-DD of the last successful verification.

fields.name: status
fields.notes: History is kept: dead and merged entries stay in the file.

fields.name: archive-url
fields.notes: Snapshot location for pages that may change or disappear.

fields.name: license
fields.notes: License or access note, including paywall or login requirements.

fields.name: annotation
fields.notes: Why it matters and when to use it. Keep under 60 words; move detail to a topic note.

fields.name: related
fields.notes: Ids or URLs of related entries, including successors of moved sources.

rules: Never delete a record; change status and record the successor in related.
A canonical URL appears once; duplicates are merged with approval and tombstoned.
Dates are ISO YYYY-MM-DD and never in the future.
High-authority entries should carry an archive-url.
Paywalled or login-only sources must say so in license.
